candidates: an office or title used in kinship descriptions
a place or estate named in titles
answers.evidence: The texts give little basis. As a separate word it occurs only in 'qore tre' (L0191) and in the fragment 'XlXi li tete li tre li tr s' (L0063, L0380; cf. 'XlXili tetelitreli yetmdelowi' in the funerary texts). It also appears as 'mlekeyos treye', beside 'mlekeyos atoye' (L0029). The verb-like 'itrek asr deb 5000 npte' ('... 5000 ... to Napata', Tanyidamani L0374.6) and the caption-like 'qore tre' ('the king offers') point weakly to giving or offering. This is a guess.

It occurs only in the proskynema formula 'tewisti are-ke NAME yeSo-a' (L0228, L0258, L0263, L0421; longer form in L0200, L0331, L0415, L0603): 'adoration' + are + the verbal ending -ke + the dedicant. The same root ar- marks capture in 'kdise-l ar(e)se-li', 'the women he took' (Akinidad stela, L0487.1-2; spelled 'arese' once). That makes 'receive/accept (the adoration of NAME)' the best fit. The alternative is 'made the adoration'.

The texts give little basis. It occurs only in the war narratives: 'abrse-l yekedi kdise-l arse-li tkk ymope/emoqe qebese-wi' ('the men killed, the women taken, tkk ...-ed them'; spelled 'tkt' once, L0487.1-2); 'qo-leb apote-bese tkk' ('these envoys' tkk', L0487.2); 'xrpxe pbo-li tkk' (L0487.5); and 'sete tkk aXotoN' (Tanyidamani, L0374.7). It comes after men and women as a third thing seized, so booty or possessions is the guess. Related forms (etkbxi, yetkbxk) could make it a verb of plundering.

candidates: Faras (Pakhoras), a town in Lower Nubia
a Lower Nubian district or governorate
another Lower Nubian town (e.g. Aniba or Karanog)
answers.evidence: It is always a place, with the locative -te, after the governor's title: 'xrpxN pXrs-te' (L0256, L0335, L0434); 'xrpxN pxrs te NAME kdite lo wi', 'she is the sister of NAME, governor in pXrs' (L0101, L0377); 'xrpxN pXrste NAME qowi' (L0085, L0521); 'mlo mrs pXrstelowi' (L0090); 'ado ws pXrs' (Kharamadoye, L0570.1). The governors of Lower Nubia sat at Faras, Greek Pakhoras, which P-kh-r-s spells.

It occurs only with large numbers in royal war stelae. 'asr axide-bx-wi 1626' and 'asr axide-bx-e-wi 1032' (Akinidad stela, L0487.4-5) close campaign sections in which captives are counted separately and only in the hundreds ('abr 32 kdi 135', 'abr 100 kdi 100', 'abr 58 kdi 223'). The Tanyidamani stela has 'itrek asr deb 5000 npte', '5000 asr ... to Napata' (L0374.6). Totals in the thousands, separate from the counts of men and women, fit herds of livestock.

The root is clearest in the Akinidad stela formula 'abrse-l yeked(i) kdise-l ar(e)se-li' (L0487.1-2, L0343.1-2): the men (abr) are killed (ked) and the women (kdi) are ar-ed, i.e. carried off as captives. The Tanyidamani stela has the same pair as 'abrse l eked kdise l erk' and 'er td' (L0374.1, L0374.7). As a separate word, ar occurs only in the Philae offering text 'ptros li s lw ar mte kw' (L0003.1, L0122, L0292.1, L0409.1, L0629.1; written 'armte' in L0004). There 'ar mte' could also mean 'male child'.

In the Kharamadoye text it alternates with Xr-w, 'northward': 'Xrw adonilikete, yireqw arw terekete, Xrw sleleke mtr ws, yireqw adereke mtr ws' (L0570.3, L0658). The same boundary formula elsewhere reads 'qeSw adereke mtr ws, Xrw pilqeke mtr ws', 'toward Kush to Adere, northward to Philae' (L0000, L0344, L0570.2). So yireqw fills the slot opposite north and carries the same directional -w.

The texts give almost no basis. It occurs only in the Akinidad stela, doubled: 'qo-leb witese yesebe ns ns-l qor ate eqepi' and 'yesebe witese ns ns-l amnp yiroX mdewi ns seb ...' (L0487.2-3, L0343.3). It stands near 'amnp yiroX', 'Amun of Napata protected'. The doubling suggests a distributive or a plural noun; the meaning is unresolved.

It behaves as a title in kinship descriptions and, like ant 'priest', takes a genitive naming a god or place. Examples: 'SSor atbo-s mleke-ye yetmde-lowi' (L0029 and 10 copies); 'SSor mn-s' (likely 'of Amun', cf. 'amnis mte', 'ant mno'), right after 'antxSxsliteb yetmdelowi' ('relative of the priests') and before 'aSore', Osiris (L0077); 'SSor lX lo wi qoreN-l', 'he is the great SSor' (L0483); 'SSor metelX-s' (L0510). The texts do not settle which office it is (priest, scribe, or other).

It follows two coordinated items: 'pqr NAME NAME tbo (yetmdelo)', 'the two princes X and Y' (L0414, L0271); 'dilX tbo woS pilqe-te-l woS tebwe-te-l', 'the two great ladies, Isis of Philae and Isis of tebwe' (L0024, L0251); 'pqr qoris NAME tboyetmdebetowi' (L0130). The Akinidad stela has the variant 'tbi' after 'pqri-li pesti-li', 'prince and viceroy' (L0487.4).

It is an epithet of Isis: 'woS mkdi woS mk di lX' (L0013), 'woS mkdi lX mk di lX' (L0018), 'woS mkdi lX' (L0251). It alternates with 'mk di lX', which is mk 'god' + kdi 'woman' (+ lX 'great'), so the phrase means 'Isis, the (great) goddess'.

It is always a place (locative -te) paired with Philae. Isis in Philae and Isis in tebwe: 'woS pilqe-te-l ... woS tebwe-te-l' (L0003.1, L0004, L0024, L0251) and 'pki woS pilqe-te-li-s-li-wi woS tebwe-te-li-s-li-wi' (L0615). Osiris in Philae and Osiris in tebwe: 'aSori pilqe-te-leb ... aSori tebwe-te-li yini-txe' (L0003.1, L0243, L0600). Isis and Osiris worshipped on the island beside Philae points to the Abaton on Bigeh, the island of Osiris' tomb.

It is kdi 'woman' + -te, used as a kin term. Examples: 'abesye kdite lX-lowi', 'elder (lX) kdite of ...' (L0009 and copies); 'xrpxN pxrs te NAME kdite lo wi', 'she is the kdite of NAME, governor of Faras' (L0101); 'pelmoS adblis NAME kdite lo wi' (L0361); 'trqlXli kditelewi trq meteli kditelowi' (L0112). Plurals: 'kditeqebetowi', 'kdite bes lo' (L0356). It is the female counterpart of wide 'brother'.

It is a title with a genitive naming its domain, listed among other officials. Examples: 'perite adb-lis NAME yetmdelowi', 'relative of NAME, perite of the land (adb)' (L0017 and copies, L0103); 'perite woS-s leb qoreN woS-s leb kdite bes lo', 'the perite of Isis and the qoreN of Isis are her sisters' (L0640, cf. L0123, L0043); 'perite woS-teb qoreN woS-teb' (L0069, L0660); 'xbxN NAME perite woS-to' (L0197). In the Akinidad stela, 'adxite perite abr 100 kdi 100' (L0487.2) may be a different use.

It is counted with dime 'cow': 'dmkte qo xlbi 3 dime 24 kelw' (L0276) and 'xlbi 3 dime 4 kelw' (L0642). A few xlbi next to many cows points to bulls. It also appears in the Tanyidamani stela's dealings with Amun ('xlbi wi', 'xlbiN', L0374.5-6).

It closes a list right before the word for the relation. Examples: 'mlekeyos treye ... mlekeyos tkreye kelw yetmde-bete-wi' (L0029); 'mrebqo kttre-leb mrebqo qoro-teb kelw yetmde aqebetowi' (L0005); 'mlekeyos p mlekeyos p kelw ye t mde bes lo' (L0638); 'a ye aqe ye kelw yetmdelowi' (L0062). It also follows counted items: 'xlbi 3 dime 24 kelw' (L0276), 'yed tlt 16 kelw yikidbitelowi s 10 kelw axide' (L0164). This makes it an additive particle meaning 'as well, also'.

'amnis mte lo' and 'mnis mte lo', 'is the mte of Amun' (L0089, L0311); 'abrs mtelo', 'mte of a man' (L0014); 'kroro bekemete mte pelmoS atolit yerike lo', 'mte begotten (yerike) by the general of the water' (L0311, L0476). Also 'mte kdi aqtoyes 2', two mte women, i.e. girls (L0315, Kharamadoye L0570.2), and 'trq mte' set against 'trq lX', junior against great (L0009).
